The US FDA has given the green light to Neuralink, the neuroscience company headed by Tesla
CEO Elon Musk, to conduct a pivotal clinical trial of its implantable brain-computer interface.
The trial, known as LINK, is intended for individuals with tetraplegia (quadriplegia), the loss of motor or sensory functions in all limbs due to a spinal cord injury.
The study protocol hasn't been made public, so the number of participants, length of trial, and endpoints are not known at this time.
In an X post, Neuralink said it has already tested the implant in more than 30 individuals.

title: Elon Musk's Neuralink gains FDA approval to conduct pivotal trial for chip implant
